verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Anytype, manage a local-first object graph with pages, collections, relations, and peer sync. The hard boundary is local-first sync protocol, mobile apps, collaboration, and identity infrastructure, plus sync, collaboration, and capture polish.
coreLoopDIY: Capture linked notes in a local-first graph of pages, collections, and relations, search them instantly, surface backlinks, sync between peers, and export a normal Markdown folder.
requirements: optional sync folder chosen by the user
whatYouLose: local-first sync protocol, mobile apps, collaboration, and identity infrastructure
ongoingBurden: file watching, conflict handling, indexing, mobile apps, encryption, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Anytype because people keep paying when the note system is trusted across every device and disappears into their daily capture habits. The recurring cost buys file watching, conflict handling, indexing, mobile apps, encryption, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: AppFlowy
priorArt.desc: Active open-source workspace with local-first documents and databases.

alternatives.name: AFFiNE
alternatives.desc: Notion and a whiteboard had one child, then let it keep files locally.

facts.install: Hosted signup or desktop app; Docker Compose for self-hosting
facts.engines: Self-hosted AFFiNE AI can be configured with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and FAL credentials
facts.dataFormat: Local-first clients keep workspace data locally and sync to AFFiNE Cloud or the operator's server; self-hosting uses PostgreSQL, Redis, and persistent blob storage
facts.gapVsPaid: AFFiNE combines documents, canvases, and databases but does not match Anytype's type-and-relation-first object graph or encrypted peer-space model.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted/desktop app installs cleanly; self-hosting is a multi-service Docker deployment that needs a domain, TLS, secrets, storage, backups, and AI-provider keys for AI features

alternatives.name: AppFlowy
alternatives.desc: A local-first workspace with pages and databases, minus the peer-to-peer mystique.

facts.install: Official desktop/mobile package, hosted signup, or AppFlowy Cloud Docker Compose stack
facts.engines: Hosted AI offers provider models including OpenAI, Google Gemini, and Anthropic Claude; local/self-hosted AI availability depends on the selected deployment and configured service
facts.dataFormat: The local app keeps workspace data on the device; AppFlowy Cloud/self-hosted sync uses PostgreSQL, Redis, and MinIO or S3-compatible object storage; pages export to Markdown or HTML
facts.gapVsPaid: AppFlowy is a Notion-style page and table workspace, not Anytype's peer-synced typed object graph with relationship-driven collections.
facts.setupBlocker: The local app installs cleanly, but self-hosting requires a sizeable multi-service stack including PostgreSQL, Redis, object storage, authentication, secrets, domain, TLS, and backups

alternatives.name: SiYuan
alternatives.desc: A block database wearing a note app's clothes, with the fiddly bits exposed.

facts.install: Desktop/mobile package, or Docker image for browser-based self-hosting
facts.engines: Built-in AI features connect to OpenAI-compatible APIs using a configured endpoint and key
facts.dataFormat: A workspace stores block documents as structured .sy JSON files plus assets on disk; SQLite files hold indexes and auxiliary state; documents can export to Markdown, HTML, PDF, and Word
facts.gapVsPaid: SiYuan is a powerful local block database but lacks Anytype's encrypted peer-to-peer spaces, object-type UX, and relationship-centric collections.
facts.setupBlocker: The desktop app installs cleanly, but free cross-device sync is not a turnkey feature: official cloud sync is a paid membership feature and Docker hosting does not transparently become desktop/mobile sync

alternatives.name: Trilium Notes
alternatives.desc: A personal knowledge tree with relations, attributes and a sync server you control.

facts.install: Desktop release package, or Docker Compose/image for a server and browser client
facts.dataFormat: Notes, hierarchy, attributes, revisions, and most attachments live in a local or server-side SQLite database named document.db; notes can be exported to HTML, Markdown, or OPML
facts.gapVsPaid: Trilium uses a hierarchical note tree and client-server sync rather than Anytype's typed object graph and encrypted peer-to-peer space model.
facts.setupBlocker: The desktop app is straightforward, but cross-device sync and browser access require operating a Trilium server, persisting document.db, and handling backups and upgrades

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Builder plan and a personal local knowledge base DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Anytype in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, and Markdown files as the source of truth; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: capture linked notes in a local-first graph of pages, collections, and relations, search them instantly, surface backlinks, sync between peers, and export a normal Markdown folder.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Store one Markdown file per note and a small SQLite index that can be rebuilt at any time.
Support wiki links, tags, backlinks, daily notes, pinned notes, and full-text search.
Add a fast command palette and keyboard-first create, rename, move, and link actions.
Render Markdown with task lists, code blocks, tables, and local image attachments.
Detect external file changes and show a safe conflict-resolution view.
Provide full-folder export, import, and an index-rebuild command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out proprietary sync servers.
Deliberately leave out real-time multiplayer documents.
Deliberately leave out a plugin marketplace and hosted public sites.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
